subject: Partner adapter convergence: request for extended deprecation and compatibility shims
messages:
From: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@lumenai.com>
To: ava_chen@redwood.ai
Cc: Opsigma Partnerships <partners@opsigma.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 16:12:00 -0800
Subject: Integration concern: upcoming API v2 enforcement and our adapter roadmap

Hi Ava,

Quick note from our integrations team — LumenAI relies on several legacy SDK endpoints that are scheduled for removal in Redwood API v2 enforcement (announced in the public changelog). We just finished mapping our connector and the attached CSV shows ~14 call sites that will break our customers.

Two asks: can Redwood either (a) extend the deprecation window for these endpoints by 9 months, or (b) provide a lightweight compatibility shim we can run in our infra to translate v2 requests back to v1 semantics? Option (b) would allow us to maintain feature parity without forcing a big refactor on our customers.

We appreciate the performance gains in v2 — we just need a workable migration path and a clear timeline to update our SDKs. Can we get a commitment on a formal deprecation timeline and whether Redwood would cooperate on the shim approach?

Attaching the compat matrix. Happy to jump on a quick call next week.

Thanks,
Sanjay
Director, Platform Partnerships
LumenAI

Attachment: lumen-compat-matrix-v1.csv (rows: endpoint, client_callsites, suggested-mapping)

From: ava_chen@redwood.ai
To: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@lumenai.com>, Opsigma Partnerships <partners@opsigma.com>
Cc: jonas_weber@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 23 Nov 2026 09:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Integration concern: upcoming API v2 enforcement and our adapter roadmap

Sanjay — thanks for the matrix and the clear ask. I've looped in Jonas (platform integrations) and Marissa (partner eng) so we can evaluate both options.

Short answer: we want to avoid indefinite extension of deprecations (security and maintenance debt), but we're open to a short-term compatibility plan that reduces lift for partners. Two paths we can offer:

- Official grace period: extend deprecation by 3 months beyond the public date, with stricter patch-only support.
- Compatibility shim: Redwood can publish an open-source translation proxy (MIT) that maps common v2-to-v1 surface-area gaps. We'll commit to maintaining the shim for 9 months from GA of v2, and provide a test harness you can run during integration.

Questions for you: which endpoints in the CSV are critical vs optional? And can your infra run a small Node/Go service in front of your adapter if we provide the shim?

If acceptable, we'll draft a short partner addendum (attachment: redwood-proposal-compat-shim-20261123.pdf) and propose a joint test schedule. Available slots for a call: Wed 25th 10–11am PT or Thu 26th 2–3pm PT.

Regards,
Ava Chen
Senior Partner Manager | Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood-proposal-compat-shim-20261123.pdf (proposal summary + maintenance commitment)

From: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@lumenai.com>
To: ava_chen@redwood.ai, jonas_weber@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 26 Nov 2026 14:08:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Integration concern: upcoming API v2 enforcement and our adapter roadmap

Thanks Ava — appreciate the quick options. We've reviewed both internally and Opsigma (our systems integrator) says the shim approach is ideal because it minimizes customer churn. A couple of follow-ups:

1) Can Redwood guarantee the shim will cover streaming response semantics and function-calling behavior differences? Those two are the trickiest bits for us.
2) If Redwood maintains the shim for 9 months, can you commit to a security patch SLA (48 hrs for critical) while it's published?
3) We want to include a clause in our referral/reseller agreement: if Redwood changes the shim mapping in a way that materially breaks our customers, Redwood will provide 60 days' notice and a co-funded migration engineering window.

We can take the proposed PDF and redline a short addendum. Wed 25th slot conflicts — Thu 26th 2–3pm PT works (we'll send a calendar invite).

Sanjay

> On Wed, Nov 25, 2026 at 10:15 AM Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood.ai> wrote:
> > Confirming internal owners for the shim dev and maintenance: Jonas will lead the shim implementation, Marissa will drive partner integration testing, Ben will own legal/contract clause tracking.
> >
> > — Ava

From: ava_chen@redwood.ai
To: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@lumenai.com>
Cc: jonas_weber@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: Sun, 29 Nov 2026 09:18:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Integration concern: upcoming API v2 enforcement and our adapter roadmap

Sanjay — quick update after our engineering sync. Jonas confirmed the shim will include: streaming proxy compatibility (chunked framing), function-calling backcompat layer (signature mapping), and request header translation for model variants. We'll publish an initial alpha on GitHub and attach a test harness you can run against your adapter.

On SLAs and contract language: Ben drafted a short addendum that includes a 48-hour critical security patch SLA for shim-maintained periods and a 60-day migration assistance clause with co-funding language. We're putting the redline into DocuSign and will share a link once internal approvals are complete.

Next steps:
- Jonas to open the shim repo and alpha release by 2026-12-06.
- Marissa to share partner test suite and onboarding checklist by 2026-12-04.
- Legal (Ben) to send the addendum in DocuSign by 2026-12-02.

If that timeline works, we'll plan a 60-minute joint integration workshop the week of Dec 13 to validate the shim against your production adapter.

Thanks — looking forward to getting this stabilized for your customers.

Best,
Ava
Senior Partner Manager | Redwood Inference

Attachment: docuSign-placeholder (will share when ready)
